content.description: 'Ven' means white/plain: unlike the sweet sakkarai pongal, ven pongal is seasoned only with pepper and cumin, not chilli or sugar. It is a staple tiffin, a common temple-kitchen dish, and the centrepiece of the Pongal harvest festival meal.
content.serving_context: Breakfast or tiffin, served hot with coconut chutney and sambar or gothsu (a tangy brinjal side).
content.cultural_notes: Frequently cooked in an allium-free temple style. The festival version is cooked outdoors in a clay pot until the milk-and-rice boils over, traditionally regarded as an auspicious sign.
